name: Asylum / Refugee Protection Claim

qualifying_event.description: A person may claim asylum/refugee protection under the Customs and Border Control Act, assessed by the Director of Customs and Border Control, with an appeal route to the Refugee Protection Appeals Tribunal (RPAT).
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Evidence of persecution risk on grounds of race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group, or political opinion.

requirements.blocker_text: Must demonstrate a risk of persecution on grounds of race, religion, nationality, membership of a particular social group, or political ideology, assessed by the Director of Customs and Border Control under the Customs and Border Control Act, with appeal to the Refugee Protection Appeals Tribunal (RPAT). Recent amendments (per reporting reviewed) raise the evidentiary standard, allow the Director to dismiss an application as unfounded based on the initial interview with no RPAT appeal (judicial review still available), and were modelled on recent UK legislation.

evidence_required.document: Initial interview with Customs and Border Control

outcome.duration_length: 3 years, per reporting on recent amendments (previously indefinite leave for successful claimants; the shorter fixed term with potential deportation if circumstances change is a recent, reported policy change, not independently confirmed against the amended Act's text)

sources.title: Cayman News Service -- reporting on amendments to the Customs and Border Control Act's asylum/refugee protection process: higher evidentiary standards, Director's power to dismiss as unfounded without RPAT appeal, 3-year (not indefinite) status for successful claimants, modelled on recent UK legislation

notes: STATUS: DRAFT, part of the Cayman Islands' initial build. The legal basis (Customs and Border Control Act, with a statutory Refugee Protection Appeals Tribunal) is real and codified, unlike Curacao where multiple human rights organisations report no functioning protection route exists in practice for Venezuelans -- Cayman's system is reported as having become MORE restrictive rather than absent, per multiple Amnesty International and Refugees International-style reports found for the broader Cayman/Cuban-migrant context in this pass (not cited here as they were not the primary source used, but corroborate that this is a live, actively-contested area of Cayman law, not a dormant provision). This route is nonetheless draft rather than published because the only source located in this pass with process-level detail is a tier-4 news outlet, not the amended Act's text itself or an official government summary -- the Customs and Border Control Act's own text was not independently retrieved in this pass despite being referenced. Treat the specific evidentiary-standard and 3-year-status details as reported, not confirmed against primary legislation.
